stem: Which one of the following statements about the role of corticosteroids in the management of children with bacterial meningitis is correct?

options.text: Corticosteroids have been shown to decrease the complication of hearing loss as a consequence of Neisseria meningitidis meningitis
As an adjunctive treatment to antibiotics, dexamethasone should be continued for 48 hours
Evidence suggests administering dexamethasone with the first dose of antibiotics
Corticosteroids have been shown to reduce mortality in meningitis caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae
Corticosteroids are indicated in all children in whom bacterial meningitis is suspected

explanation: Dexamethasone is given as an adjunct to antibiotics and should be administered before or with the first antibiotic dose, as benefit is reduced if started later. It is not indicated for all children with suspected bacterial meningitis, and it has not been shown to reduce mortality overall.
rationale: Preserves the best existing option: dexamethasone should be administered with the first dose of antibiotics.

optionExplanations.A: Steroids are not specifically shown to reduce hearing loss after meningococcal meningitis.
optionExplanations.B: The key issue is timing with antibiotics; this statement is not the best correct answer.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Dexamethasone should be given before or with the first dose of antibiotics.
optionExplanations.D: Adjunctive corticosteroids may reduce some complications in selected cases, but not mortality as a general rule.
optionExplanations.E: Steroids are not indicated in every suspected case of bacterial meningitis.
